title: AI Is Now the Fed's Top Financial Stability Worry
dek: 87% of market contacts in the Fed survey named AI as a risk to the system.

facts.label: Survey contacts naming AI as a risk
AI computing debt issued by Oct 2026
Outstanding public debt tied to AI compute

caption:
Wall Street has a new number one fear, and it's AI. 📉

In the Federal Reserve's Financial Stability Report released November 13, 2026, 87% of market contacts surveyed by the New York Fed named artificial intelligence as a risk to the U.S. financial system, far ahead of any other threat. In the spring, AI ranked only third.

The worries fall into three buckets: sky-high AI stock valuations, AI-powered cyberattacks, and tangled financing behind the data center boom. Debt issued for advanced computing passed $680 billion by October, about five times all of 2023, and the Fed compares spending by Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle to the late-1990s telecom buildout.

The Fed still calls the banking system sound and resilient, but the real fear is clear: AI profits may not keep pace with AI spending. We break down what it means for your savings and business at AI Parabellum.

post_caption:
The AI boom now has a $1 trillion question attached to it. The Fed estimates outstanding public debt tied to advanced computing tops $1.1 trillion, and big U.S. banks have close to $1 trillion of exposure to big tech, data center developers and utilities.

No crisis alarm yet, but regulators are clearly following the AI money trail.
